task.description:
WF-03 Step 0.5 (registry lookup) + Step 1 (diagnose) for ISS-0911 (queue task 903, GH#2037), combined. ISS-0891 (already resolved, PR #2017, commit d2bb3817, merged to main -- confirmed present in the current tree) fixed a race where the wrong/stale definitionId was SUBMITTED on Start despite the UI showing the correct version -- fixed by adding a synchronous startDefinitionId state. ISS-0911 reports a DIFFERENT-shaped symptom in WF05-FULL2-20260930: the read-only start-definition-version DISPLAY field itself stayed EMPTY for 10s in 5 of 6 untraced (fast) runs, while the one traced (slower, more instrumentation overhead) run passed. This symptom shape (display empty until a slow async resolution completes, worse without trace-induced slowdown) suggests the version TEXT shown to the user may be bound to a different, still-async source (e.g. a query/fetch for activeDefinitionByName's version, separate from the startDefinitionId fix) that has not itself been synchronized -- read InstanceBoardPage.tsx's full version-display binding (not just the startDefinitionId submission path ISS-0891 already fixed) to determine this.

Step 0.5: check docs/issues/ for other resolved entries with a similar 'version field empty/stale' symptom before this one -- none expected beyond ISS-0891 itself.

Step 1: (a) Confirm ISS-0891's fix is genuinely present in the current code (already spot-checked by ORCH: startDefinitionId exists, lines ~77-112, 208, 228 of InstanceBoardPage.tsx -- verify fully yourself). (b) Trace exactly what the read-only version-display field's own value is bound to -- is it activeDefinitionByName?.version (a query result) or startDefinitionId-derived, and does THAT binding have its own unsynchronized async gap the ISS-0891 fix didn't address? (c) State explicitly whether this is (i) a genuine residual code-side race requiring a further fix, or (ii) purely a QA-deployment-lag question this repo cannot determine (the fix is in main but QA's deployed build may predate it) -- in which case state that plainly as the diagnosis rather than fixing speculative code, since ISS-0911's own filing text says 'QA exposes no build SHA, so first confirm the ISS-0891 fix is actually deployed' and this checkout has no way to query QA's live deployed commit. If your best determination is (ii), do NOT implement a speculative fix -- report this and let ORCH route to a no_defect/instrumented-style close per WF-03's own vocabulary (see docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md's status vocabulary) rather than guessing at code that may not even be the problem. If (i), give CODE-DESIGNER a precise description of the additional race to close.
acceptance_criteria: ISS-0891's fix (startDefinitionId) is independently reconfirmed present and correctly wired, with exact line citations
the version-display field's actual data-binding path is traced and named explicitly (which state/query/prop it reads from)
a clear determination is made: residual code race (i) vs. undeterminable-from-this-repo QA-deployment-lag question (ii) -- not left ambiguous
no speculative fix implemented if the determination is (ii)

result.summary: Step 0.5: grepped docs/issues/*.yaml for 'version'/'empty'/'race' symptoms beyond ISS-0891 -- none found; ISS-0891 is the only prior match, already cited by ISS-0911 itself. This is NOT a same-root-cause recurrence (see below) -- it is a different, previously-unaddressed race in the same file/flow, so no severity bump per the recurrence rule. Step 1: (a) ISS-0891's fix independently reconfirmed present in web/src/pages/instances/InstanceBoardPage.tsx: dedicated `startDefinitionId` state declared at line 77 (with its own explanatory comment lines 65-76 citing ISS-0891), set synchronously alongside `startDefinitionVersion` in the mount/definitionId-change effect (lines 104-112), in `openStartDialog` (lines 164-175), and in `onStartDefinitionNameChange` (lines 181-200); `submitStartInstance` (lines 202-239) validates and submits `startDefinitionId`, not `definitionId`, at lines 208 and 228. Confirmed correctly wired -- ISS-0891's fix is genuinely in this tree, not a deployment question for that specific defect. (b) Traced the version-DISPLAY field's actual binding: the read-only input at lines 452-466 is `value={startDefinitionVersion}`, a local useState (line 64). Three write sites set it: the effect at 104-112 and `openStartDialog` at 164-175 both derive it from `activeDefinitionByName?.version` (a `useDefinition(definitionId)` query keyed on the PAGE-level `definitionId` URL search-param, line 90-92) -- irrelevant to this repro since the e2e spec never touches the page-level filter. The one path that matters for ISS-0911's repro (fresh /instances navigation, dialog opened, process key typed directly into the dialog's own 'start-definition-name' input) is `onStartDefinitionNameChange` (lines 181-200): it looks up `exact = definitionTypeahead?.items.find(item => item.name === value)` and, ONLY if found, synchronously sets both `startDefinitionVersion` and `startDefinitionId` together (so ISS-0891's own fix is not implicated here -- both are already set atomically in this path). The bug is upstream of that pairing: `definitionTypeahead` (line 85-88) comes from `useDefinitions({ status: 'ACTIVE', name: definitionName || undefined })`, and `definitionName` (line 50) is read from the PAGE-level `searchParams.get('definitionName')` -- the page's own filter box (id='instance-definition-filter', lines 341-356) -- NOT from `startDefinitionName`, the dialog's own local state the user is actually typing into (line 63, bound to the dialog input at line 434-447). Typing into the dialog never changes `definitionName`/the page's URL param (only an exact match found via `onResolveDefinition`, the PAGE filter's onBlur handler at 140-151, would do that), so `definitionTypeahead` is fetched once with `name: undefined` and never refetched as the dialog's input changes. `definitionsApi.list()` (web/src/api/definitions.ts lines 15-17) hits a cursor-paginated endpoint (`CursorPage<ProcessDefinition>`) with no `page_size`/`cursor` passed, i.e. only the backend's default first page of ACTIVE definitions tenant-wide. Whether a just-created process (created moments earlier by the pipeline's own pre-step, per platform-definition-promotion-rollback.pipeline.e2e.spec.ts lines 136-159) appears in that first page depends entirely on how many ACTIVE definitions already exist for the tenant and their sort order -- neither guaranteed to put the newest entry first. Repeated e2e/pipeline runs against a long-lived QA tenant accumulate ACTIVE definitions from prior runs (random-UUID process keys, never archived), so the odds of a fresh definition falling outside the default first page rise over the environment's lifetime -- independent of, and not fixed by, ISS-0891's startDefinitionId change. This also explains the observed shape: when `exact` is not found, `onStartDefinitionNameChange`'s else-branch (lines 196-199) sets `startDefinitionVersion`/`startDefinitionId` to empty/undefined and nothing thereafter retries the lookup, so the field stays empty until the 10s Playwright assertion timeout, not merely 'delayed'. (c) Determination: (i) GENUINE RESIDUAL CODE-SIDE RACE / QUERY-SCOPING BUG, independent of ISS-0891 and NOT a QA-deployment-lag question -- the mechanism is fully visible and reproducible by reading this repo's current source; no data about QA's deployed build SHA is needed to reach this conclusion, because the bug exists in the currently-checked-out code regardless of what QA is running. The one traced/passing run out of six is consistent with this: it is exactly the kind of environment-population-dependent non-determinism (whether the freshly created definition happens to land in the default first page) this mechanism predicts, not evidence that timing/instrumentation overhead itself fixes anything. WHAT A FIX MUST CHANGE: the dialog's typeahead-matching in `onStartDefinitionNameChange` must resolve the typed name against a definitions list actually filtered/queried by the value the user is typing in the DIALOG (`startDefinitionName`), not the page-level filter's `definitionName` -- e.g. by querying `useDefinitions({ status: 'ACTIVE', name: value })` (or an existing debounced/dedicated lookup by exact name, such as `definitionsApi.getActive(name)` at web/src/api/definitions.ts line 22-23, which resolves the single active definition for a given name server-side without relying on any paginated list membership) at the point the dialog's own input changes, rather than reusing the page-scoped `definitionTypeahead` query whose `name` filter is bound to a different piece of state entirely.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design: resolve the Start Instance dialog's 'start-definition-name' exact-match lookup (InstanceBoardPage.tsx onStartDefinitionNameChange, lines 181-200) against a definitions source actually scoped to the dialog's own typed value (e.g. definitionsApi.getActive(name) or a useDefinitions call keyed on startDefinitionName), replacing reliance on definitionTypeahead (queried by the page-level definitionName filter, lines 85-88) which can omit a just-created/just-activated definition once the tenant's ACTIVE definitions exceed the backend's default list page size. This is independent of, and does not touch, the already-correct ISS-0891 startDefinitionId synchronization.
